articles.title: Valkyries fall in OT as Wings' Ogunbowale scores 45 to force Game 3 at Chase
articles.summary: The Golden State Valkyries were looking to finish off their series with Dallas, but the host Wings didn't cooperate Wednesday, winning 108-100 to set up a de...
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas - The Golden State Valkyries oppressive defense had a momentary lapse. That bit of breathing room was all Arike Ogunbowale needed to put together one of the best playoff performances in WNBA history.

Ogunbowale was operating with desperation. Her Dallas Wings were facing elimination at home on Wednesday, and the Valkyries had their way with the No. 7 seed in Game 1. She poured 45 points on a Valkyries defense that prides itself on stifling anyone in its path. Her 45 points are the most scored in any playoff game in WNBA history, beating the record by three points.

Each point was needed in a wire-to-wire overtime game the Wings claimed 108-100 at College Park Center, tying the first-round series 1-1 with a deciding Game 3 to be played Friday night at Chase Center.

"I think our energy was different," Golden State 's Gabby William s said. "I didn't recognize us tonight. I don't think any of us did."

Here are takeaways from the Valkyries' loss.

Defensive lapse: The Valkyries appeared to ramp up the pressure early, picking up where it left off from Game 1. Williams picked up Paige Bueckers full court, mucking up the Wings' spacing and forcing a handful of turnovers early.

3-Point Goals: 12-27, .444 (G.Williams 5-12, Thornton 3-4, Burton 2-4, Charles 1-2, Zandalasini 1-2, Salaun 0-3).

Turnovers: 10 (Hayes 3, G.Williams 2, Burton, Charles, Salaun, Thornton, Zandalasini).

Steals: 8 (G.Williams 4, Burton 2, Zandalasini 2).

3-Point Goals: 12-23, .522 (Ogunbowale 5-8, Clark 3-4, James 2-3, Kuier 1-2, Bueckers 1-4, Siegrist 0-1, Sims 0-1).

Team Rebounds: 15. Team Turnovers: None.

Turnovers: 13 (Ogunbowale 5, Shepard 3, Kuier 2, Bueckers, James, Siegrist).

Steals: 6 (Ogunbowale 3, Bueckers 2, James).

But then the Wings started to pick up their pace and the Valkyries' were late reacting, resulting in lackluster defense and 28 fouls committed on their end. The 108 points are the most points Golden State has allowed in franchise history and the 93 points in regulation are a season high.

"I didn't recognize us, but more importantly we don't give up 108 points," head coach Natalie Nakase said. "That's just completely uncalled for. I have to do better. I have to do better in terms of getting on them quicker. I can communicate and make more of timeouts quicker."

Any defensive lapse can prove fatal for the Valkyries. That is their identity. Without a star scorer, their league-best defense is what separates them from the herd.

The Wings got Bueckers off the ball and recently-named Most Improved Player Jessica Shepard, and others, take the ball up. A porous perimeter - which Golden State usually has on lock - opened up driving lanes for Ogunbowale, who got aggressive and confident early on.

Ogunbowale finished the first half with a team-high 16 points and took off from there, finishing 12-for-23 from the field and 5-for-8 from 3-point range. Eleven of those points came in overtime.

Her biggest shot came with the Valkyries up three in the final 14 seconds of regulation when she drained rainbow over Kayla Thornton 's outstretched arms, reminiscent of the National Championship game-winning fadeaway 3-pointer she hit for Notre Dame in 2018. It was a far cry from her 10-point performance in Game 1.

"We just felt like we got pushed around out there when we played in San Francisco," Ogunbowale said. "I didn't feel like I was aggressive. … I just think I was being really passive and wasn't playing my game."

Nakase called Ogunbowale's game "brilliant," but after the loss fixated on how the Valkyries could have forced her to her weaker side.

"We know she likes that step back left, so that's what was really frustrating," Nakase said. "We know she likes to step back left, and we didn't get to it. We didn't force her to the right."

The Valkyries got into some foul trouble early on - Veronica Burton and Kaila Charles fouled out in overtime - and Ogunbowale was the beneficiary. She went to the line 18 times and made 16 free throws. The Wings were 32-for-37 from the line while Golden State was 20-for-23.

Dallas' bench filled the gaps. Alysha Clark and Aziaha James were the primary scorers other than Ogunbowale. Clark chipped in 21 points and James 13. Bueckers went quiet, scoring 10 points.

From a grueling overtime loss Golden State can perhaps find solace in the nature of the outcome. It took a historic performance and an overtime fight for Dallas to notch their first win of the year against Golden State. Ogunbowale's performance will be difficult to replicate.

Williams and bench: The Valkyries kept up because Williams was aggressive early looking for her shot. She created her own offense primarily and scored 18 points by the half and led the team with 36 points on 12-for-23 shooting from the field. She shot 5-for-12 from 3.

Thornton along with key bench contributions helped drive the second-half push. The Valkyries reclaimed the lead behind Thornton, who scored seven points in the third quarter's first few minutes and took a hard foul doing it.

Charles locked in toward the end of the frame, making a 3 and a driving layup at the buzzer to get the Valkyries a two-point lead entering the fourth quarter.

But the Valkyries couldn't get enough scoring from anyone other than Williams to overcome a confident Ogunbowale.

articles.title: 49ers news: Zach Allen calls Trent Williams the GOAT before Broncos clash
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers All-Pro left tackle Trent Williams continues to serve as one of the most important pillars of the team’s offense. However, Denver Bronco...
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers All-Pro left tackle Trent Williams continues to serve as one of the most important pillars of the team's offense . However, Denver Broncos defensive lineman Zach Allen believes Williams' standing extends far beyond his role with the 49ers.

During Wednesday's press conference ahead of the 49ers' upcoming matchup against the Broncos , Allen offered the ultimate compliment to Williams, calling him the best tackle to ever play in the NFL.

"I have all the respect in the world for Trent. I, honestly, I know you see the debates about who's the best. I think he's the best tackle of all time," Allen said via Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The 49ers acquired Williams through a trade in 2020 as they looked to find a replacement for legendary offensive tackle Joe Staley . Since joining San Francisco , Williams has established himself as a dependable fixture on the team's offensive line and has remained a key presence throughout his stint in the Bay Area.

Beyond his elite play on the field, Williams has also provided valuable veteran leadership. His presence has been closely associated with the 49ers' sustained success, which includes multiple NFC Championship Game appearances and a trip to the Super Bowl. San Francisco rewarded Williams for his continued importance by giving him a two-year, $50 million extension this offseason. The contract ensured that the All-Pro left tackle remains under contract with the franchise through the 2027 season.

However, Allen's glowing assessment of Williams comes at an important point in the 49ers' season. Williams briefly left the team's previous game after suffering a neck stinger, creating some concern about his availability for the upcoming matchup. Still, head coach Kyle Shanahan attempted to ease those concerns by indicating that Williams " should be good to go by Thursday, " according to David Lombardi.

Hopefully, Williams will be able to suit up against Denver, giving Allen and the Broncos a chance to test themselves against the player the defensive lineman considers the greatest tackle in NFL history.

articles.title: Biggest takeaways from Steelers' Joey Porter Jr. trade with Cowboys
articles.summary: Here's a look at the biggest takeaways from the Joey Porter Jr. trade involving the Pittsburgh Steelers and Dallas Cowboys.
articles.body:
Joey Porter Jr. , no longer a Pittsburgh Steeler , has been traded to the Dallas Cowboys in exchange for multiple draft picks from the 2027 and 2028 NFL Drafts. The Steelers opted to (finally) put an end to the Porter saga in Pittsburgh, leaving a few key takeaways to consider following the trade.

From the emergence of another starting cornerback to pondering if a trade was really the best move for Pittsburgh's 2026 roster, here's a look at several takeaways from the Steelers-Cowboys Porter trade.

Did Asante Samuel Jr. lead to Porter's exit?

Out of any of the Steelers on rookie deals heading into the 2026 offseason, Porter appeared to be the most untradeable. Or so we thought. Perhaps the Steelers' decision to part ways with a premium lockdown cornerback was made easier by the stellar play of Samuel at training camp.

After the Porter deal, the Steelers and Cowboys have completed three separate trades in the past two years. Pittsburgh traded George Pickens to Dallas in May 2025 and Broderick Jones just before final roster cuts in August 2026. Considering the Cowboys have basically given up only two third-round draft picks and one second-round draft pick to land Pickens, Jones, and Porter, the Steelers don't exactly look like the winners in these deals.

Many speculated that Porter's back injury had more to do with contractual drama than an actual health setback. After missing the first three games with a conditioning and back injury designation, Porter was still able to entice the Cowboys to give up a premium draft pick in 2028. If there was more to his absence than the injury designation suggested, which many believe to be the case, the Steelers may have let Porter walk all over them in this situation without so much as a single fine.

The Steelers held all the cards in the Porter situation, but now their roster is in worse shape in what's supposed to be Aaron Rodgers ' boom-or-bust retirement tour with head coach Mike McCarthy. Paying Porter would've likely been the better move. Calling his potential bluff on the back injury and fining him should've been the next step if he refused to play. The Steelers also had a franchise tag option to use to restart negotiations following the 2026 season. Unfortunately, general manager Omar Khan decided it was best to pull the plug on arguably the Steelers' best man-coverage cornerback in the past decade.

articles.title: Heartbreak at Man Utd as ‘exciting’ Red returns to Carrington with torn ACL
articles.summary: Manchester United youngster Jack Moorhouse has returned to the base prematurely after suffering a nasty injury.The 20-year-old has been one of the most inter...
articles.body:
Manchester United youngster Jack Moorhouse has returned to the base prematurely after suffering a nasty injury.

The 20-year-old has been one of the most interesting prospects to emerge from the club's academy over the past few years.

After last season's experience at Leyton Orient, the midfielder attracted interest from Dundee FC, who signed him on loan on the summer transfer market's deadline day.

Man Utd youngster Jack Moorhouse sustains serious ACL injury

Moorhouse made his debut in the Scottish Premiership with a 45-minute appearance against Hearts, who beat Dundee by two goals to one.

The following game, the youngster was in the starting lineup, helping the Dark Blues beat Motherwell 2-1.

Sadly for the MUFC loanee, this may have been his last appearance for Dundee, as The Courier reveals that the player has sustained a 'devastating' injury.

Moorhouse thus returned to Carrington to undergo the required clinical tests. The results confirmed the worst, and the Ireland U21 international is now set for a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

As the source explains, Moorhouse is curiously the third Dundee player to suffer an ACL injury since the start of the season, as his teammates Simon Murray and Fin Robertson had suffered similar fates.

Can Moorhouse recover from this major career setback?

(Photo by Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

Unfortunately, ACL tears are becoming increasingly common in football. These injuries are widely considered the most devastating for athletes, as they require a long and agonising rehabilitation program, and many fail to regain their pre-injury form.

As for Moorhouse, he is described in the report as an 'exciting' young player who managed to show 'flashes of real quality' in his two appearances in Scotland .

Therefore, we can only hope that the young midfielder overcomes this hurdle and returns stronger next season.

That being said, it won't be easy for the youngster to bounce back after potentially losing an entire season at this crucial stage of his development.

articles.title: Red Sox’s Garrett Crochet Decision Backfires; Adley Rutschman Doesn’t Help
articles.summary: The Boston Red Sox took a chance. Garrett Crochet has been an All-Star in the major leagues, and so with him back from injury after a long absence and Boston...
articles.body:
Garrett Crochet has been an All-Star in the major leagues, and so with him back from injury after a long absence and Boston's backs against the wall, they tried him out at Yankee Stadium on Wednesday night.

He allowed a run while on the mound and exited with the bases loaded and no out — three more runners his responsibility as Garrett Whitlock trotted in to try and rescue things.

Crochet had been "worth the gamble," NBC's broadcasters agreed. It didn't pay off, though.

The irony here is incredible: It looked like Crochet got the first batter he faced out.

He struck out Spencer Jones swinging. It should've been one up, one down.

But the ball got away from catcher Adley Rutschman , and on the dropped third strike, Jones could try and beat a throw to first.

Rutschman's throw initially got Jones called out, but a replay review overturned it and called Jones safe.

So Crochet had a strikeout, but not an out.

Jones then stole second and advanced to third on a throwing error by Rutschman.

That's when George Lombard Jr. delivered an RBI single for a 3-1 Yankees lead.

After Lombard, Jazz Chisholm Jr. singled through the right side, and then Trent Grisham bunted for a single.

It wasn't really a bunch of bad stuff done by Crochet by any means.

But after four batters, Crochet was out of the baseball game.

Rutschman had never caught Crochet in a game before.

The Red Sox traded for Rutschman in the middle of the season, in a long stretch when Crochet was away from the mound with an injury.

Rutschman was a big gamble by the Red Sox to improve their catcher position, and in general, it has worked.

But it's fair to wonder if his unfamiliarity with Crochet hurt him on his miscues while Crochet was on the mound.

Everything happens very fast, and so it's not even to say Rutschman should've made the plays that were there for him. But it's clear that he played a role in the inning being rough for Crochet.

And it was the kind of inning that might decide Boston's season. Maybe they weren't going to score again anyway, and if that was the case, they weren't going to win anyway.

But when you add these Yankees runs, and in this manner against Crochet, it certainly made everything a bit tougher.

articles.title: Mavericks news: Dusty May makes intriguing comment on Dallas starting unit
articles.summary: Entering the 2026-27 NBA season, the Dallas Mavericks are facing a lot of uncertainty surrounding the top five names who will be the starters for the team....
articles.body:
Entering the 2026-27 NBA season , the Dallas Mavericks are facing a lot of uncertainty surrounding the top five names who will be the starters for the team. And rookie NBA coach Dusty May is not stressing about the issue.

May addressed the speculation surrounding Dallas' first and second units Wednesday, saying the Mavericks are still focused on smaller lineup combinations rather than establishing a starting five.

articles.title: Joe Espada 'absolutely' wants to return as Astros manager, but awaiting chat with owner Jim Crane
articles.summary: The Astros won the AL West for the second time in three years under Joe Espada but another quick playoff ouster leaves the manager's future uncertain with no...
articles.body:
With the Houston Astros eliminated from the playoffs, Joe Espada said he "absolutely" hopes to return as manager but has not been given any indication about his future.

Espada is not under contract beyond this season, his third year as Houston 's manager. The Astros were eliminated Wednesday in the wild-card round by the White Sox , who concluded a sweep of the best-of-three series with a 7-3 win at Daikin Park .

Afterward, Espada said he had not been told anything about his status but that he expected to "have a conversation" with Astros owner Jim Crane "in the next day or two."

"Jim has been very clear about his process and when he wants to have that conversation," Espada said. "I respect the process and how blessed I've been to be here for over nine years and experience so many division titles, championship series, World Series, winning one. As a bench coach, as a manager, I have witnessed so many great moments. So obviously, I would like to continue enjoying those moments."

On Aug. 24, Crane dismissed general manager Dana Brown , who like Espada was in his final year under contract. Brown promoted Espada from bench coach , a role he held for six seasons for Houston , to the manager job after the 2023 season.

Crane said in August that Espada would remain manager for the rest of the season and the team would decide on his future "at the end of the season." At the time, Crane stated that his "expectation" was for the Astros to win the American League West.

Houston did that, albeit with an 81-81 record in a division where no other team finished above .500. It was the fourth straight season the Astros posted a declining win total. They have not won a postseason game since 2023, swept in two wild-card series since then by the Tigers and White Sox.

"He showed up every day wanting to win," second baseman Jose Altuve said of Espada on Wednesday night. "I think he did everything he could to keep us there to keep winning … This is a team, we all work together. I think we're all sad. Like I said, we wanted to go to the World Series and win it."

Flawed roster construction factored into this season's results. The Astros' pitching staff had the seventh-highest ERA in the majors, their outfielders ranked 29th of 30 teams in OPS and they started 19 different pitchers, a franchise record. They won the AL West for the eighth time in 10 seasons.

Whether that will keep Espada in his role is unclear. Crane told the Associated Press this week that the Astros making the playoffs "would be something to consider" when deciding on Espada's future. But a two-game sweep by the White Sox put an abrupt end to their hopes of a run.

"Joe was great for us," shortstop Jeremy Peña said. "Joe is a stand-up guy, stand-up man. He shows up every single day, he wants to win, he works hard. And I think he did everything in his power to be the best version of himself, be the best manager for his players."

The Astros have finished with 88, 87 and 81 wins in their three seasons under Espada. The franchise's streak of eight straight playoff appearances ended in 2025 , when they finished one win shy of a berth. They started 20-31 this season but recovered to clinch the AL West on the season's final day.

"For myself, I know that Joe was with us every step of the way and he was going to do everything he could to put us in the best position to succeed," starter Hunter Brown said. "I think that's exactly what he did."

Espada on Wednesday night dismissed the notion that it was difficult to manage this season without clarity about his future.

"No, it's part of the job," Espada said. "You've still got to win on the baseball field and deliver what the expectations are."

After pushing to secure a playoff spot for the season's final two weeks, the Astros never led in the two wild-card games against the White Sox. They fell behind 3-0 after two innings in Game 1 , when both teams ran bullpen games, and trailed 4-0 in the first inning of Game 2 , a deficit they never erased. The end of their season came with uncertainty about their manager's future.

"I've been blessed," Espada said. "I've been here for a long time. And I've been in a few piles, I've been soaked in Champagne. I have created some really great relationships. I have witnessed some Hall of Fame players that I've coached and I've … been part of some really special years.

"That's every coach, every manager's dream is just to be able to coach and lead players like this in an organization that gives you the opportunity to always get the best players so you can consistently win divisions and go to the World Series. I've been part of that and I'm just blessed just to be part of it."

After a disappointing playoff exit, there was a lot of chatter surrounding the future of the Denver Nuggets . Jamal Murray , who has been with the team since 2016, found his name thrown into trade rumors and scenarios. Despite all the talk, Murray has not paid much attention to it.

"It's a business at the end of the day," Murray said. "I've been blessed and grateful to be with the same team that drafted me."

During the end-of-season press conference, team president Josh Kroenke said any Nuggets player is on the table for trade talks, except for three-time MVP Nikola Jokic . Even with the Nuggets being a bit non-committal about Murray's future, he is still heading into the upcoming season excited to play alongside his teammates.

"Personally, I'm grateful just to be here and have an opportunity to win a championship with my brothers," Murray said. "We've been (through) ups and downs and all that stuff. To have this type of relationship, even off the court, it means a lot."

Murray is coming off a career year. He hit career highs, averaging 25.4 points, 4.4 rebounds, and 7.1 assists per game while also shooting 43.5% from 3-point range. To top it off, he earned his first All-Star and All-NBA selections.

Aaron Gordon , who was sitting alongside Murray at Nuggets media day, has witnessed his teammate's talent firsthand.

"This is a master at his craft. He can't shoot the ball any better," Gordon said. "He can't dribble the ball any better. Everything is maxed out. This is one of, if not the, best shot makers in the game today."

Murray and the Nuggets will open up their preseason on October 4 against the Utah Jazz .

articles.title: Once an imperfect fit, Luis Garcia Jr. becoming crucial to Yankees' World Series aspirations
articles.summary: Luis Garcia Jr. was not a perfect fit for the Yankees when they traded for him, but the first baseman has become a crucial part of the team's aspirations of...
articles.body:
Luis Garcia Jr. was not a perfect fit for the Yankees when they traded for him.

They needed an offensive catcher and relievers, and maybe a guy who could hit more than the people they had playing third, depending on one's perspective. But a lefty-hitting first baseman with defensive limitations? They already had a few of those.

And yet, with a Division Series bid at stake against their most ancient rivals, Garcia delivered a resounding fourth-inning homer that broke a scoreless tie -- exactly what the Yankees needed. He finished with a three-hit night.

"My mom has a good saying. She's always telling me never stop dreaming," Garcia said through an interpreter before the game. "…Having this opportunity to be here, being able to go out there and be part of the playoffs, go out and represent the Yankees, it feels great. And just hoping that I'm able to go out there and do the little things that can help us keep winning."

When the Yankees weighed options at the deadline, they had a perfectly functional first base situation that centered around Ben Rice and made room for Paul Goldschmidt against tough lefties. With Giancarlo Stanton on the way back from injury, they did not plan to have at-bats to spare at designated hitter, so they looked ill-equipped to navigate a logjam.

But Garcia was the best bat available -- at least of those players who were actually traded -- so they added him to a lineup that sometimes resembled a revolving door, but sometimes would need to revolve around him.

Garcia seemed to adjust to New York quickly. He was born here and grew up a Yankees fan, so playing at Yankee Stadium was aspirational, not intimidating. The 26-year-old isn't the type to stress much anyway. His demeanor is as easy as his swing and just as level. He hit .290 with an .842 OPS in August. He did not look overwhelmed.

Then, just as the Yankees began their final push for the postseason, Garcia stumbled into a vexing slump. He hit .105 with a .255 OPS and no extra-base hits in their last 10 games. The contact savant struck out 11 times in 38 at-bats. He pinch-hit in Game 1, his first career postseason at-bat, and grounded into a double play.

Aaron Boone chose to hit him third in Game 2 of his first ever playoff start anyway. And with the game still scoreless in the fourth, he clicked. He pulled a homer to right center that gave the Yankees the lead before singling twice more – once to left, once to right, a perfect display of the evolution that has turned him into a crucial piece of a World Series contender.

In the early years after the Nationals signed him, Garcia earned comparisons to Juan Soto , not necessarily because of his style, but because of his talent. Then, as now, Garcia had incredible bat-to-ball ability -- a smooth flick of the wrists he designed to mirror Robinson Cano and succeeded.

But through parts of six major league seasons, some of which Nationals officials later admitted probably came before he was ready, as they filled needs instead of prioritizing development, Garcia never quite emerged as the star he seemed capable of being. He hit for a high average as a Nationals regular over the last three seasons, but he settled for hitting pitches because he could get his bat on them instead of prioritizing clobbering.

That changed this year when an overhauled Nationals coaching staff and front office encouraged him to choose more pitches he could drive while also helping him use his lower half to move the bat instead of just relying on his hands.

"I think the biggest difference has to be using my back leg in a better way to help me generate more bat speed. Previously, since I think I was able to use my hands, the quickness of my hands and rely on that more," Garcia said through an interpreter. "But I worked really hard on incorporating my lower part of the body, especially my back leg, and I think that's what helped me get to where I am today."

Garcia's average bat speed jumped dramatically, from 72.4 miles per hour in 2025 to 74.3 miles per hour in 2026 – a jump that moved him from the 98th fastest in baseball into the top 50. He started pulling the ball in the air far more than he ever had before, and damage followed: Garcia's .831 OPS was the highest of his career by more than 50 points.

"Part of his success this year is he's a more mature player today," said Amed Rosario , who played with Garcia in Washington in 2025. "He's made adjustments over the years, and it's showing. The talent is there, but I think that's why he's having such a great season."

Rosario said he tried to help ease Garcia's transition to the Yankees -- one Garcia admitted he was anxious about in the hours after being traded.

"All the teammates that you're leaving behind, all the relationships you've built over the years, you're leaving behind and you're starting from zero," he said. So coming in, you feel a little afraid, if you will, that you have to do that over again. But I can tell you that from the moment that I walked into the clubhouse, that went away, that fear went away very quickly because the guys make me feel as part of this team immediately."

Now, Garcia looks at home in New York, where he is surrounded by family so much that he said recently it reminds him of being in the Dominican Republic.

"The energy we have in this team, the fans, the clubhouse, everything that is part of this team, it's a great spot to be here at this moment," Garcia Jr. said after the game.

As his interpreter shared his answer, Rosario and a handful of teammates interrupted. It was time to shower the newest Yankees hero in Budweiser and champagne.

articles.title: Golden State Warriors Praised for Bringing Back Veteran Guard in Free Agency
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors had a very quiet free agency, bringing in just two role players.The Warriors did re-sign six veterans, drafted Yaxel Lendeborg and...
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors had a very quiet free agency, bringing in just two role players.

The Warriors did re-sign six veterans, drafted Yaxel Lendeborg and secured Steph Curry for two more seasons with a new extension.

But one of the Warriors' moves was recently praised for being "under the radar."

Warriors Praised for De'Anthony Melton Signing

GettyDe'anthony Melton #8 of the Golden State Warriors dribbles the ball against the Los Angeles Clippers at Chase Center on March 02, 2026 in San Francisco, California.

According to NBA.com's Jeff Zillgitt , the Golden State Warriors re-signing De'Anthony Melton to a two-year, $12.3 million contract is one of the 10 best "under the radar" moves of the 2026 offseason.

"In 49 games last season, Melton averaged a career-high 12.3 points and matched a career high in steals per game (1.6)," Zillgitt wrote. "He struggled with his shot last season as he returned from an injury that limited him to six games in 2024-25. But before last season, he shot at least 37.1% on 3-pointers in five consecutive seasons. Now that Melton is fully healthy, the Warriors believe he will return to that percentage."

Melton's numbers improved in the second half of the season, especially when his minutes increased during Steph Curry's absence due to his runner's knee injury.

The 28-year-old guard is expected to come off the bench this upcoming season. However, he will likely be called upon to score more and be an alternate playmaker if Curry gets rested or misses time due to his recurring knee issues.

Zillgitt's list also includes players like John Collins to the Detroit Pistons , Tim Hardaway Jr. to the Miami Heat and Kelly Oubre Jr. to the Indiana Pacers , among others.

Speaking to reporters during Monday's media day, De'Anthony Melton shared that his left knee is feeling well heading into training camp. Melton is going to be a full participant and won't have any limitations.

The veteran guard also explained how different his regimen was this summer compared to when he was rehabbing from his left knee surgery.

"It's a little different," Melton said via NBC Sports Bay Area . "But I think every year and every summer, I used to kind of go through not necessarily a rehab stage, but a time where you work on managing your body and making sure you're reaching tip-top shape once the season rolls around. For me it was just more so just maintaining and getting strengthened in certain areas."

With Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody out to start the season, coach Steve Kerr will look for Melton off the bench to provide additional spark on both sides of the floor.

articles.title: Ohio State vs. Iowa prediction, odds, pick for Big Ten clash in Week 5
articles.summary: Ohio State faces its first major Big Ten test when Ryan Day and his Buckeyes travel to Iowa City to take on the undefeated Hawkeyes. The Buckeyes (3-1, 1-0 i...
articles.body:
Ohio State faces its first major Big Ten test when Ryan Day and his Buckeyes travel to Iowa City to take on the undefeated Hawkeyes. The Buckeyes (3-1, 1-0 in the Big Ten) come into this game feeling with a positive feeling about the Hawkeyes — at least prior to kickoff. Iowa (4-0, 1-0 in the Big Ten) comes into this game after a heart-stopping, last-play-of-the-game victory over Michigan. The Wolverines are Ohio State's hated rivals, and the Buckeyes get a warm feeling any time Michigan loses a conference game.

The Buckeyes known that they have serious business to take care of against an opponent that has proven to be opportunistic and tough when the game is on the line. Iowa routed two opponents but has had close wins against in-state rival Iowa State and the Wolverines.

The Buckeyes let their tough Week 2 game at Texas slip through their grasp when they let a big lead get away in the fourth quarter. Day has put the blame for that game on himself, and there was a lack of killer instinct shown by Ohio State when Julian Sayin, Jeremiah Smith and Bo Jackson had a chance to put the game away.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

It will be a party atmosphere at Kinnick Stadium when the Hawkeyes come out of the tunnel, because the home team will have a chance to beat Michigan and Ohio State in back-to-back weeks. However, the Buckeyes have far more offensive talent than the Wolverines, and their early-season loss means they are not likely to be careless when the game reaches its crucial moments.

Ohio State is a far more dynamic offensive team than Iowa, and should be able to dictate the pace if it can get an early lead.

Ohio State — CB Jay Timmons (questionable), ORT Philip Daniels (questionable), TE Bennett Christian (questionable)

Iowa — DB Tyler Brown (out), DB Kyler Gerardy (out), DB Darion Jones (questionable), LB Derek Weiskopf (questionable)

– Iowa is 3-1 against the spread this season.

– Iowa is 6-4 ATS as a home underdog in their last 10 games in that category.

– Ohio State is 6-3 ATS as a road favorite in their last 9 games in that category.

– The Buckeyes lead the all-time series against Iowa, 48-15-3.

– Ohio State's largest margin of victory in the series is 62 points.

– The Buckeyes' longest winning streak in the series is 16 games.

– Iowa's largest margin of victory is 31 points.

– The Hawkeyes' longest winning streak in the series is 2 games.

Ohio State certainly knows how to go into a hostile environment and figure out how to play their best game. They may have lost at Texas in the second game of the season, but the Buckeyes dominated the game early and built a 23-3 lead through three quarters.

They have the athletic ability, talent and experience to not fall victim to a late rally for the second time this season. It starts with quarterback Julian Sayin and wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. Both are Heisman Trophy candidates and that could actually hurt either player when it comes to winning the award because they could take votes away from each other.

That's of little concern as they prepare for this game. Sayin is having an excellent year as he has completed 83 of 115 passes for 1,206 yards with 10 TDs and 1 interception. Smith is the best receiver in the nation and he ranks with the top receivers that have ever played at Ohio State. He has caught 33 passes for 617 yards with 7 touchdowns, including a 72-yard TD reception against Illinois last Saturday.

The Buckeyes have a number of studs on the offensive line, and the running game includes Jackson and Ja'Kobi Jones. Jackson has rushed for 283 yards while averaging 5.7 yards per carry and Jones has 206 yards and is averaging an eye-opening 6.6 yards per carry.

The Hawkeyes will come into this game with plenty of momentum after their 20-19 triumph over Michigan. Quarterback Hank Brown threw a perfect pass to Reece Vander Zee in the end zone on the final play of the game. They quieted a thunderous crowd at Michigan Stadium and handed the Wolverines their first loss of the season.

The Hawkeyes are one of the top defensive teams in the Big Ten as has are allowing just 239.8 yards per game. Head coach Kirk Ferentz knows his defense can't shut Smith down completely, but they will try to limit his big plays.

Iowa's offense came to life in the late stages of the win over the Wolverines, and Brown will try to get the best of Ohio State's defense. Brown has completed 66 of 97 passes for 700 yards with 5 TDs and no interceptions. RB Kamari Moulton has rushed 284 yards and he has a shocking 7.3 yards per carry average on his 39 rushing attempts.

Ohio State has the same goals as it always does. Win the Big Ten title, beat Michigan and win the national championship. In order to accomplish those goals, they can't let a tough game on the road stand in their way. The loss to Texas means there is very little margin for error and a loss in this game would be disastrous since they have a huge game against defending national champion Indiana in two weeks. Iowa will come at Ohio State with an improving offense, but Ohio State will win the game. However, Iowa rewards its backers with the cover.

Final Ohio State vs. Iowa Prediction and Pick: Iowa +14.5 (-110) and Under 45.5 (-110)

articles.title: Luis Díaz reflects on his first Bayern Munich season
articles.summary: Díaz enjoyed a fabulous 2025/26 in FC Bayern colors.
articles.body:
Changing clubs and changing leagues does not always make for the smoothest of transitions — as Bayern Munich fans know well. But last summer's arrival of veteran winger Luis Díaz from Liverpool could not have gone much better than it did. The Colombian international acclimated immediately, was a fixture in Vincent Kompany's XI, and notched 26 goals and 19 assists across all competitions as Bayern set and chased goals records domestic and abroad.

"It was a very, very special year for me. Coming here, to this great club, was truly spectacular," Díaz reflected during his interview with Sky Sport journalist Kerry Hau, as captured by @iMiaSanMia . "I was given an incredibly warm welcome. From the very first day, my teammates made me feel as though I had already been here for many years, and that was of course very important to me. I settled in quickly and felt comfortable.

"My family was also very quickly very happy here. And that's important as well. So I hope to stay here at FC Bayern for many more years and that we can continue winning lots of titles. That's what matters most to me: having goals and achieving them, with this great and special club."

Díaz certainly enjoyed a productive inaugural season in Bavaria. While this year's campaign has not gotten off to the same blistering start, it is surely only a matter of time before Díaz gets hot again.

articles.title: Wales have absolute belief despite form - Ampadu
articles.summary: Ethan Ampadu says Wales have "absolute belief" in their approach as they look to end a demoralising run by beating Norway in the Nations League.
articles.body:
Ethan Ampadu says Wales have "absolute belief" in their approach as they look to end a demoralising run by beating Norway in the Nations League.

Wales' winless run has stretched to six matches after defeats in their opening League A fixtures in Portugal and Denmark.

Though they make a welcome return to the Cardiff City Stadium, the task does not get any easier as Wales take on Erling Haaland and company on Thursday (19:45 BST) before Sunday's return fixture against Denmark.

But Leeds United captain Ampadu insists there is no doubt within Craig Bellamy's injury-hit squad that they can compete at the top level.

"You aren't in the team meetings or the dressing room, but if you saw how we train and prepare, you'd see complete belief in what we are doing," Ampadu said.

"When you go through difficult spells and tough results, it might be natural for outsiders to question that, but one thing we've always been good at - even during the hardest matches - is resilience and sticking together.

"We know the last couple of games weren't us, and there is complete confidence across the group that we can put that right."

Wales emerged from last week's 1-0 defeat in Lisbon with some credit, having run a star-studded Portugal side close despite being without the likes of Karl Darlow, Joe Rodon and Harry Wilson.

But Bellamy's men endured a dispiriting night in Copenhagen, when they were well beaten by a Denmark side who lost 3-2 in Norway seven days ago.

The latest setbacks mean that in eight games across two spells in Nations League A, Wales have suffered seven defeats and taken only one point, from a home draw against Belgium in June 2022.

Despite the record, Ampadu insists Wales' players "have full confidence in what we can achieve" – and says they want more than victory alone against Norway, who were quarter-finalists at this summer's World Cup.

"We want a win, but we also want a performance to be proud of," the 65-cap star said.

"In recent games, we haven't looked like ourselves. It hasn't been our identity, it hasn't been what we're good at, and it wasn't what earned us promotion to Nations League A in the first place.

"A win will naturally boost everyone's mood, but it has to go hand-in-hand with a display that represents our true identity."

articles.title: Somerset pair Overton & Luff take top PCA awards
articles.summary: Somerset pair Craig Overton and Sophie Luff win the top prizes at the Professional Cricketers’ Association awards.
articles.body:
Somerset pair Craig Overton and Sophie Luff have won the top prizes at the Professional Cricketers' Association awards.

Overton, the men's player of the year, had a stellar season across formats as Somerset just missed out on a first County Championship title and reached the semi-finals of the T20 Blast.

Luff becomes the first winner of the women's player of the year award not to have played international cricket since 2021. As well as superb form in county cricket, the 32-year-old was part of the Trent Rockets team that won The Hundred.

Pace bowler Sonny Baker and left-arm spinner Tilly Corteen-Coleman won the two young player of the year awards.

All-rounder Overton, 32, scored three first-class hundreds and averaged less than 20 with the ball in the County Championship.

His form has led to talk of a recall to the England team to fill the vacancy left by Ben Stokes, four years after he won the last of his eight Test caps.

Overton beat off other shortlisted nominees Joe Clarke, George Hill and Dan Lawrence.

"It's a phenomenal feeling," said Overton. "To be chosen by your peers to win this award is very special, it means so much to me.

"I felt like I got in a groove where my body was in a good spot, not 100% because of the schedule, but mentally I felt like I was in a great spot to be able to go out and perform when games come along near enough every other day."

Somerset captain Luff scored more than 1,000 runs across formats during the summer, including averaging in excess of 40 in the One-Day Cup.

Luff triumphed ahead of three internationals on the shortlist – Maia Bouchier, Sophia Dunkley and Mady Villiers.

"I've always been a leader that wants to lead from the front, but I think people are seeing that play out in games now," said Luff. "I think this year I've just showcased what I'm capable of.

"I've had a new role at Somerset opening the batting and it's safe to say it's gone pretty well and I've probably unlocked something to bring the best out of me as a player. I'm so grateful to all my team-mates and coaches at Somerset that have supported me."

Baker, 23, made his Test debut against New Zealand at The Oval in June. He was part of the Manchester Super Giants team that won The Hundred and the Hampshire side that reached the final of the T20 Blast.

Corteen-Coleman, 19, was a surprise inclusion in the England squad for the T20 World Cup.

Former England captain Heather Knight was given the Outstanding Contribution Award following her international retirement.

Another international retiree, Tammy Beaumont, won a Special Merit Award.

articles.title: Youthful Man United Women smash Durham 5-1 to seal third win in a row
articles.summary: 1Manchester United Women won their third match in a row as they beat Durham 5-1 away from home in the Players’ Cup.First halfThe Red Devils opened the scorin...
articles.body:
Manchester United Women won their third match in a row as they beat Durham 5-1 away from home in the Players' Cup.

The Red Devils opened the scoring in peculiar fashion as the ball was played into the box from a corner by Jess Simpson and the ball almost seemed to hit Rebeca Bernal and loop into the net, with the Durham defender applying the last touch.

It was Bernal's third goal in a week, as the Mexican appears to be loving life in a red shirt.

Surprisingly, Durham were level just minutes later when Janina Leitzig inexplicably let Lucy Watson's dipping free kick drop into the bottom corner of the goal.

Maya Le Tissier and Ellen Wangerheim responded with efforts at goal, but they could not find an opener before half-time.

Lea Schuller's header and Jess Simpson's long-range drive also asked questions of the Durham defence, but with no result.

United had to wait until the 58th minute, but they finally got what they were looking for.

Dominique Janssen stepped up and hit a sumptuous free kick that gave the Durham keeper no chance, restoring Eva Olid's side's lead.

A few minutes later, new signing Monica Jusu Bah made sure of the points. The Swede danced past two defenders before unleashing a fine effort into the bottom corner with her left foot.

The next goal was one hundred percent made in Carrington as a long throw from Scarlett Hill was flicked on by Layla Drury and Mared Griffiths showed great instinct in the box to latch onto the loose ball in the area and smash it past the keeper for the visitors' fourth.

Finally, United grabbed a fifth in injury time when great work down the right by Jess Anderson saw Elisabeth Terland poke in the cross and keep United top of the Players' Cup standings.

United will next be in action on Saturday afternoon when they host Liverpool at the Progress with Unity Stadium.

articles.title: ☀️ Juve keen on Solet, Pulisic renewal, Taylor off? Morning news

articles.body:
The long international break continues, with the weekend approaching along with the final two fixtures for national teams around the world.

The news, however, does not stop. Let's take a look at the most important stories of the morning.

Juventus are very active in the free-agent market and, according to Tuttosport, there are several names on sporting director Massara's radar. Among the most complicated, but also the most interesting, are Oumar Solet and Stanislav Lobotka.

As reported by the source, Juventus are very keen on both players, but Udinese and Napoli have a unilateral option to extend their contracts.

Milan , Cardinale wants to tie down Pulisic ! The details

Milan have rediscovered Pulisic and Cardinale's objective is to tie down the American. How? With a renewal that months ago seemed certain and then was put on hold.

As reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport, the Rossoneri have an option for one more year but Cardinale wants an agreement until 2031. A few years ago, Pulisic asked for €5 million to extend: that figure could be the one, or even higher.

Inter , focus on new deals for Dimarco and Carlos Augusto

Inter, after tying down Pio Esposito and Bisseck, have final meetings on the agenda to get Federico Dimarco and Carlos Augusto to sign new contracts.

As reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport, there has already been a meeting regarding an extension for the Italian until 2030. For Carlos Augusto, whose deal expires in 2028, the goal is to extend it by at least a few more seasons, with a salary increase of course.

Napoli, positive signs from the treatment room

Napoli could have reason to smile after the break thanks to the returns of injured players. Buongiorno will be back at the end of the year, but McTominay has already trained on the pitch.

There is also news on Marianucci, who hopes to be available when play resumes, as does Leonardo Spinazzola , who will return against Frosinone to compete for a starting spot. This is according to La Gazzetta dello Sport.

Roma, Ndicka back in the starting lineup?

After being left out against Inter to make room for Balerdi , the door to a starting role with Roma could reopen for Ndicka. His physical problems are behind him and with the national team he has returned to being a leader.

As reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport, he could get the nod again against Como , with Gasp called upon to choose and rotate.

Kenneth Taylor continues to impress at Lazio and there could be developments in January.

As reported by Il Messaggero, he could be the expendable name to generate a capital gain, with possible approaches in the winter market.

Nicolò Fagioli, Fiorentina and Italy midfielder, spoke to Rai. Here are his words.

"My dream right now is to go to the World Cup with Italy. It's my biggest dream."

Are you still the boy from "Fragile," the documentary that introduced you to people, or are you a different person now, changed and more mature compared to when it was filmed?

"I've matured a lot, especially on a human level, because certain things make you grow. I'm much more confident in myself, bolder in some things and also tougher in others. I think that has been the biggest change in me."

articles.title: MLB should be terrified of Yankees as Aaron Judge gets ready 'fast as I can'
articles.summary: Yankees made quick work of their rivals. What does that mean for the rest of the field?
articles.body:
NEW YORK — Aaron Judge always has the best vantage in any room, one of many perks that standing 6 feet, 7 inches affords a man. And as Wednesday turned to Thursday and September gave way to October, he could be found near the back of the New York Yankees ' clubhouse, watching the champagne shoot and the beer fly in the room before him.

The New York Yankees celebrated this conquest – a two-game sweep of the rival Boston Red Sox in their American League wild-card series, capped by a 9-2 Game 2 rout – in the usual fashion, albeit a bit abbreviated. The lights came on before midnight, halting the party and reminding them there's a plane to catch and an AL Division Series matchup with the division champion Tampa Bay Rays on deck.

Beyond surviving and advancing, though, there was something grander to celebrate: The Yankees played a postseason game without Judge for the first time since 2015 – and not only did they move on, they flourished.

Judge, their three-time AL MVP, sat out from June through mid-September this year due to a rib fracture. The Yankees won 93 games, anyway.

Judge suffered a calf strain in the final week of the season and, through gnashed teeth, sat out this wild-card series as his comeback attempt fell just short.

The Yankees put on a punishing display of all-around excellent baseball without him, crushing the Red Sox by an aggregate 18-2 score over the two games and certainly making the Rays sit up in their easy chair and take notice.

Until ALDS Game 1 Saturday at Tropicana Field, the Yankees, their fans and the news media will engage in two more days of will-he-or-won't-he, right up until ALDS rosters are released. Even with a little liquid courage – most of it worn on the skin rather than down the gullet – Judge stopped well short of predicting his availability.

"I'll be ready," he said, "as fast as I can."

Judge loves to play coy, though he's not nearly as good as it as he probably believes. Yet he could not suppress his satisfaction at the manner in which "his boys," if you will, fileted the Red Sox:

Starting pitchers Cam Schlitter and Max Fried combined to give up one run in 12 1/3 innings, and their staff held the Red Sox scoreless the first 14 innings of the series.

Shortstop George Lombard Jr. had four hits in the two games, the first Yankee since, yes, Derek Jeter to record four hits in his first two playoff games.

Cody Bellinger and Ben Rice , the lineup bulwarks in a Judge-less Yankee universe, combined for three home runs and 10 RBIs; each had crucial fifth-inning hits on consecutive nights to turn a 1-0 Yankee lead to 2-0, only to follow with back-breaking bombs later.

And the Yankees ran wild in Game 2, stealing four bases, Spencer Jones keying a six-run sixth inning by lumbering down to first after striking out on a passed ball. They laid down bunts for base hits, guided line drives into the outfield rather than swinging wildly for the fences and strafed the Red Sox bullpen.

2026 MLB playoffs open with thrilling wild-card series matchups

At 34, Judge is more than a decade older than some of his teammates. And sitting out this series gave him the chance to contextualize what he saw, a 10,000-foot view that looked downright picturesque.

"It's incredible to see the resilience out of those kids," says Judge. "It doesn't matter the situation. Guys are stepping into bigger roles and accepting it and owning the moment.

"We all talked about it before this series started: The teams that play the cleanest baseball are going to be the ones who win these series and move on. That was our main goal. If we could clean up our bunting stuff, our baserunning stuff, our defense, moving guys over.

"These two games here, guys came up with some big hits for us. Guys got put in some tough situations and prevailed. I think we're just going to really lean on those situations and take it into a tough opponent in Tampa ."

Wanna talk about a contrast? How about the way the Yankees went out in 2024, getting punked by the Los Angeles Dodgers in a five-game World Series defeat, losing Game 5 when Judge dropped a fly ball, a gaffe he said would "stay with me until I die ."

These Yankees played excellent baseball, a byproduct of a deep roster that can morph into whatever manager Aaron Boone needs it to be.

Consider that in that 2024 Series, the left side of the infield was Anthony Volpe at shortstop and Jazz Chisholm at third, a combo that combined for a key error in that decisive Dodgers rally.

In 2026? They are a second-base platoon, Volpe yielding to Lombard and remaking himself into a utilityman after a humbling stint in the minors.

In Game 2, Chisholm got the start as Boone rolled out a lineup with eight left-handed hitters. It is what they can do with a roster this deep and Boone is pushing all the right buttons even in the face of significant injuries.

"It's taken all of us, in that regard, to overcome the challenges. We've found a way to thrive with a hand behind our back and (Boone) is a big part of it," says former Cy Young Award winner Gerrit Cole , who will start Game 1 of the ALDS. "Brian Cashman is a big part of that, too. You've got to go out and buy the tools.

"The roster looks really good at this point. We're very competitive and we have a lot of different ways we can beat you."

That wasn't the case in 2023, when the season went south after Judge suffered a significant toe injury and was limited to 106 games. The Yankees went 82-80 and stayed home for the playoffs.

"Aaron has been hurt for a good portion of the year," says Cole, "and we still figured out a way to play good baseball. I think we've learned some things from it."

And gained some talent from it. Judge's injury prompted Cashman to acquire outfielder Heliot Ramos and infielder Luis Garcia Jr. at the trade deadline. Garcia ripped a fourth-inning homer in Game 2 to break a scoreless tie. He had three hits, and is perhaps best emblematic of the club's depth that Cole can only laugh when he notes they have three first basemen – Rice, Garcia and Paul Goldschmidt – somehow on a 26-man roster.

"It's a great spot to be here, in this moment," says Garcia, who had not played in the postseason until this series.

Even better if No. 99 is around for the next one. Judge had been largely invisible this week, opting not to get introduced on the baseline before Game 1. Yet he let himself get drilled with booze along with his teammates, even if he did not tangibly contribute.

"I'm wearing a Yankees uniform. I've got NY on my chest," says Judge. "When the Yankees win, we all win. Doesn't matter if you played, didn't play, got the game-winning hit, pitched a shutout.

"We're all wearing NY and we're all celebrating together."

And perhaps Judge will be playing with his boys come Saturday. If not, well, October is a long month. And the view from Yankee Stadium only looks better and better.

articles.title: Cowboys news: 2 other NFC teams showed interest in Joey Porter Jr
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys won the Joey Porter Jr sweepstakes. That said, they were not the only NFC teams tracking the Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback before his st...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys won the Joey Porter Jr sweepstakes . That said, they were not the only NFC teams tracking the Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback before his stunning departure. According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report, the Detroit Lions and New York Giants also expressed interest in acquiring Porter as Pittsburgh's contract stalemate with the defensive back reached a breaking point.

Schultz reported that the Steelers determined in recent days that an agreement was no longer realistic after extension talks stalled ahead of Week 1. That ultimately prompted Pittsburgh to move the former first-round selection . Detroit and New York both explored the possibility of upgrading their secondaries . Dallas, though, emerged as the most aggressive and persistent suitor. The Cowboys ultimately sent Pittsburgh a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-rounder for Porter. Now, Dallas adds a physical perimeter presence to a secondary dealing with early-season injuries.

His ability to play press coverage should give the Cowboys defense another weapon opposite DaRon Bland while adding needed size and physicality outside. The move also reunites Porter with former Steelers teammates George Pickens and Broderick Jones in Dallas. That's after the Cowboys have made multiple notable transactions involving Pittsburgh.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Porter entered the NFL as the No. 32 overall pick in the 2023 draft. He quickly established himself as a physical boundary corner. He became a full-time starter midway through his rookie campaign and earned PFWA All-Rookie Team honors. His 34-inch arms and aggressive press technique have since helped him develop into a disruptive perimeter defender. Now, Dallas is betting that Porter can become a long-term anchor in its secondary.
